clips.title: Hands on skin
clips.listen: Two hand drums. Bass, ghost taps, slaps and open tones are one drum hit in different places with different parts of the hand. Bar 2 mutes two tones (hand stays on). Bar 4: one drum is squeezed so its pitch talks, then a finger roll and a last bass.

clips.title: Hollow log, clay pot
clips.listen: A wooden tongue over a box: each note is a slow doublet with the air inside, so it wobbles as it dies; rim clicks and muted notes are the same mallet elsewhere or staying down. Under it a clay pot whose pitch is the air in it: whoops up when the hand leaves the hole, sags when it closes. A scrape leads into bar 3; the log grows more hollow to the end.

clips.title: Friction and thunder
clips.listen: A wet finger rubbed on a skin: a moan at the skin's own pitch that follows the squeeze (no oscillator, the friction sticks and slips). It is answered by a huge slack skin: hit hard, the pitch starts high and settles, an air boom sits an octave under it, and loose beads rattle until the skin calms. The last pot note is bent by a hand over the hole while it rings.

clips.title: One bar, tight to cavernous
clips.listen: The same bar four times while the family macro travels from tight to cavernous: the skin goes slack (pitch glide on hard hits, boom under the tone, beads from bar 3), the log turns hollow and slow, decays lengthen. Same notes, same velocities.

clips.title: For comparison: the existing rack on clip 1
clips.listen: The notes of "Hands on skin" on the closest sounds the rack already had: context kick for the bass strokes, context snare for the slaps, the dead-marimba bar for open tones and the escapement clock for ghost taps. Four different machines, each note identical to the last one like it; nothing answers how or where it is hit, nothing can be muted, squeezed or rolled.

clips.title: One phrase, whisper to feral
clips.listen: The same phrase three times. First barely blown: the note is air until it finds itself, and it wanders. Then plainly: tongued starts, legato moves without a new attack, a scoop in, a fall out. Then pushed: harder embouchure, the reed itself buzzing in the sound, throat growl, a bark on the top note.

clips.title: Gestures
clips.listen: Bar 1: a deep scoop, then a slow slide up a fifth under one breath. Bar 2: flutter-tongue, a growled note, a long fall. Bar 3: six tongued repeats of one pitch (accents, soft ones nearly air: no two alike), then a legato run. Bar 4: a low note pushed until it breaks into its upper register.

clips.title: Two held notes
clips.listen: Nothing but two long notes. The first is ridden on the breath: from air into tone, swelling until the throat growls, a lip bend down and back, vibrato arriving late, then let go. The second opens its register vent halfway (a split tone), closes it, and ends on flutter-tongue.

clips.title: Reed over hands (both families)
clips.listen: The two families together, briefly: the hand-drum bar and a pot bass under a reed line that leans into the drum's slaps. Not a song: four bars to hear them share a room.

clips.title: For comparison: the existing rack on clip 1
clips.listen: The phrase of "whisper to feral" on the closest sound the rack already had, the Impossible Voice in its hollow, reed-like "hollow-whistle" setting, cold then hot. It is a sung vowel made by adding partials: it can glide and fall, but there is no breath pressure to lean on, no reed to push shut, no tongue, growl or register break.
